title: Per-table ALTER from the field repository
summary: Makes one Firebird table match the field repository: exact DDL, refused or lossy changes blocked before anything runs, dry run by default
intro: Read this when a column changed in the field repository and the Firebird table must follow. drag-lint repo alter-table prints the exact DDL for ONE table, blocks what Firebird would refuse or would accept and lose data on, and writes only with --apply, after its own pre-checks on the same connection and a verified backup of the database. An opt-in safe path (add, copy, compare, swap) does the changes Firebird refuses.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint repo alter-table --table <T> --direction repo-to-db --connection "<Firebird connection string>" (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--safe-path] [--rename <OLD=NEW[,...]>] [--order <A,B,...>] [--hook <name>] [--code-dir <folder>] [--server-dir <folder>] [--client-dir <folder>] [--select <id file>] [--apply] [--dry-run] [--backup-dir <folder>] [--backup-name <name>] [--verify <full|quick>] [--json]
help: drag-lint repo alter-table    --table <T> --direction repo-to-db --connection "<Firebird connection string>" (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--safe-path] [--rename <OLD=NEW[,...]>] [--order <A,B,...>] [--hook <name>] [--code-dir <folder>] [--server-dir <folder>] [--client-dir <folder>] [--select <id file>] [--apply] [--dry-run] [--backup-dir <folder>] [--backup-name <name>] [--verify <full|quick>] [--json]   (make ONE Firebird table match the repository; prints the change set with the exact DDL and writes NOTHING without --apply; a change Firebird refuses, or accepts and loses data on, is BLOCKED; drops, DROP NOT NULL, safe-path changes and the widening of a column other objects use are unchecked: name their ids, after the plan line of the dry run, in --select; all in that file never takes a drop; with --hook micronite a successful --apply is followed by a DRY RUN of repo update-orm for the table (it uses --code-dir / --server-dir / --client-dir) that lists the ORM units that would change, a failure of it only warns; --apply first makes a backup (a server on another machine needs --verify quick), restored and compared unless --verify quick, see repo backup --connection; --safe-path offers add-copy-compare-swap for refused type changes; --hook micronite = the Micronite rules; exit 0 ok, 1 bad arguments or a refused or failed apply)

drag-lint repo backup         --connection "<Firebird connection string>" [--verify <full|quick>] [--table <T>] [--backup-dir <folder>] [--backup-name <name>] [--project <project file>] [--json]   (a backup of the DATABASE through the Firebird service API, as DLFR_BACKUP_<database>_<yyyymmdd>_<hhnnss>.fbk unless --backup-name gives the name (a name not a path, .fbk added, an existing file is never overwritten); restored into a temporary database and compared unless --verify quick; free space checked first; a server on ANOTHER machine is allowed with --verify quick given explicitly: it writes the file on its own disk, the host and that path are printed and recorded as NOT verified (remote, not verified), the free space is not checked, --backup-name is refused there (exit 1 before connecting: the automatic time-stamped name is used so nothing is overwritten), and purge never deletes it; recorded in %LOCALAPPDATA%\drag-lint\db-backups.json)

drag-lint repo backup         list [--connection <..>] [--json] | purge --keep <N> [--connection <..> [--apply]] [--dry-run] [--json]   (the recorded backups; purge is a dry run without --apply and deletes only backups of the database --connection opens, only recorded files whose size and date did not change, and never the newest or the newest verified one)
